chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Yahya, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Speech is of three types: truth, lie, and reconciliation between people.

It was said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is the reconciliation between people?' He said: 'You hear speech from a man, which reaches him and makes his soul feel bad. Then you meet him and say, 'I heard from so-and-so that he said good things about you,' which is the opposite of what you actually heard from him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of reconciliation between people in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) categorizes speech into truth, lie, and reconciliation (islah), defining the latter as strategically conveying a positive report opposite to what was heard to soothe feelings and resolve conflict. This concept, known as *islah* or *tadlis al-haqq* (veiling the truth for peace), is distinct from outright lying (*kidhb*) because the core message remains beneficial and non-deceptive in intent, serving as a practical tool for social harmony in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Yahya Al Wasity, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The speech are three (types) – a truth, and a lie, and a reconciliation between the people’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘It was said to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>! What is the reconciliation between the people?’

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘You hear speech from the man, had it reached him (the other one), it would have made him feel bad. Then you meet him, so you are saying, ‘I heard from so and so saying regarding you, such and such from the goodness’, opposite to what you had actually heard from him’.
en.sarwar: 16. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from abu Yahya al-Wasiti from certain individuals of our people from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Statements are of three kinds: true, false and to establish truce among people.’

The narrator has said that it was asked of him, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, what is establishing truce among people?’ The Imam said, ‘It is when you hear something about a man that, if he himself may hear it, his soul turns filthy (with anger) but when you meet him you say, ‘I heard so and so saying very good things about you, which is opposite of what you have actually heard about him.’”
